meta.triageRationale: One cohesive story under a single design (the approved SPEC-77932eaa1a85819b + mocks), but with real design choices and several build tasks: a new companion page shell + pan/zoom runtime, a header-context resolver (project name / work-item id / source doc id / git user), per-type plug-ins for the four definitions in src/workflow/artifacts/companion, additive optional description/narrative fields on four JSON schemas with LOW findings, prompt/schema updates for the design-story and design-epic synthesizers, and orchestrator finalize wiring. It touches 1-2 modules (src/workflow/artifacts/companion plus the orchestrator finalize call sites) and must NOT regress the docgen tool, which also calls assembleShell (src/docgen/index.ts:118), so the companion shell is separate. Not an epic: no new subsystem and no independent stories; not small: >1 file, schema changes, several tasks.

summary.prose: Every companion page the workflow generates (ER model, UX mock, sequence diagram, component dependencies) is rendered through one companion-owned page shell instead of docgen's diagram shell and the separate UX emitter. The page has a header (project name, work item, source doc, date, user), a narrative (a context line from the source document plus the visual's own narrative), a view panel with one pan/zoom for every visual, and per-type description tables. Each definition module supplies only typed page content; the shell owns layout, escaping and the inlined runtimes. The ER visual becomes a real entity-relationship diagram and sequence arrows carry their real labels; definitions gain optional description and narrative fields whose absence raises a LOW finding.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Standalone feature — no parent HLD. Design directly against the repo, grounded on the s1 analyze passes. There are no HLD shared contracts to honour.

boundary.internal: Render every workflow companion through one shared page template

dataModelChanges.details: New type in src/workflow/artifacts/companion/types.ts: { projectName: string; workItemId: string; sourceDoc: { id: string; href: string }; date: string; user: string; contextLine: string }. Resolved once per finalize site by a new header module: projectName = `<repo>/.insrc/config.json` key `projectName` when a non-empty string, else basename(repoPath); workItemId = safeCanonical(() => <epic or story workflow id from epicHash, anchorCreatedAt, storyId>) (src/workflow/id.ts), falling back to the plain storyId (LLD) or epicHash (HLD) when the minters would throw on a malformed createdAt / epicHash / storyId; sourceDoc.id = hldArtifactId / lldArtifactId, href = './' + basename(source md); date = injectable clock formatted 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm' local time; user = `git config user.name` in the repo, else os.userInfo().username, else 'unknown'; contextLine (deterministic, per the SPEC 'Epic/Story placement plus HLD Summary or Story statement'): for an HLD source, 'Epic <slug>' + the first sentence of the HLD body.summary.prose; for an epic-Story LLD, 'Story <Snnn> of Epic <slug>' + the Story's title and userValue first sentence read from the Epic's DEF (the same DEF the LLD finalize already resolves); for a standalone LLD, 'Standalone story <Snnn>' + the story title persisted in body.hldContextSlice.boundary.internal (set from the triage storyTitle by standaloneStoryContext in src/workflow/runners/design-story/standalone.ts) and the first sentence of the LLD body.summary.prose. When none is available the line is placement only.

New type returned by a pure per-kind builder in each of er.ts / ux.ts / sequence.ts / component.ts: { kindLabel: string; narrative?: string; visual: { kind: 'mermaid'; source: string } | { kind: 'html'; html: string }; description: readonly DescriptionBlock[] }. DescriptionBlock = { heading?: string; lead?: string; columns: readonly string[]; rows: readonly (readonly DescriptionCell[])[] }, DescriptionCell = string | { tag: 'pk' | 'fk' | 'call' | 'return' | 'marker'; text: string } | null (null renders as an em dash). The UX html visual is produced by the existing card emitter in ux.ts (already escaped); every other string is escaped by the shell.

Optional `narrative?: string` on the definition; optional `description?: string` on ErClass and on ErSlot. ER_DEFINITION_PROPERTY_SCHEMA gains the same optional properties. validateErDefinition validates against the VENDORED, CLOSED LinkML subset (src/assets/artifacts/schemas/linkml-metamodel.schema.json: additionalProperties:false at root, ErClass and ErSlot), so that asset must also gain `narrative` (root, string), `description` (class, string) and `description` (slot, string); without it every definition using the fields would get a HIGH 'LinkML metamodel violation' and finalize would re-prompt forever. `narrative` is an insrc extension (not LinkML-native); `description` is LinkML-native.

dataModelChanges.details: The validators (validateErDefinition, validateUxDefinition, validateSequenceDefinition, validateComponentDependencyDefinition) KEEP their documented contract (an EMPTY array for a sound definition) and are not changed. A new pure function per kind, `completenessFindings(def)`, returns at most two LOW DimensionFindings: one when `narrative` is absent, one listing the elements missing a `description`. It is called ONLY from the code-review diagram/ux dimensions (diagram/handlers/er.ts, sequence.ts, component.ts and ux/index.ts), so the LOWs surface in the code-review record where authors see them; they are LOW so they never block. firstCompanionValidationFailure and finalize are unchanged (they never see these findings).

errorCases.scenario: The vendored Mermaid bundle or the new pan/zoom script is missing from out/assets at render time.
errorCases.detection: The shell's runtime loader catches the readFile ENOENT when loading the asset manifest or bundle.
errorCases.response: Throw DiagramGenerationError('fallback-unavailable', <asset + copy-assets remedy>); the existing finalize helpers already catch it and leave the definition in-body without a picture.
errorCases.userImpact: The artifact is written without that companion link; a warn log names the missing asset.

errorCases.scenario: `git config user.name` fails (git missing, not a repo, or no user configured).
errorCases.detection: execFile rejects or returns an empty/whitespace stdout.
errorCases.response: Fall back to os.userInfo().username; if that throws (no passwd entry in a container), use 'unknown'. Never throws out of the header resolver.
errorCases.userImpact: Header shows the OS login or 'unknown' instead of the git name.

errorCases.scenario: `<repo>/.insrc/config.json` is unreadable or not valid JSON, or `projectName` is not a non-empty string.
errorCases.detection: readFile/JSON.parse throws, or typeof check fails.
errorCases.response: Ignore the override and use basename(repoPath); log at debug.
errorCases.userImpact: Project name falls back to the folder name.

errorCases.scenario: Mermaid fails to render the emitted source in the browser (e.g. an unexpected character in an entity or message label).
errorCases.detection: The inline init script's mermaid.run promise rejects.
errorCases.response: The page shows a visible 'diagram render failed: <error>' line inside the view panel; the header, narrative and description tables still render because they are static HTML.
errorCases.userImpact: Reader still sees all tables and text; only the picture is missing.

errorCases.scenario: Work-item identity cannot be minted (malformed createdAt, epicHash or storyId in meta).
errorCases.detection: The minters behind deriveWorkItemIdentity throw (id.ts workflowId validation); the header resolver calls them through safeCanonical, which returns undefined.
errorCases.response: Use the plain storyId (LLD) or epicHash (HLD) as the Work item value; the header resolver never throws, so finalize (which rethrows anything but DiagramGenerationError) is never aborted by header resolution.
errorCases.userImpact: Header shows a shorter work-item id; the companion still renders.

edgeCases.input: A definition with no `narrative` and no element descriptions (every pre-existing definition).
edgeCases.expected: Page renders with only the context line in Narrative and em dashes in every description cell; completenessFindings returns two LOW findings (surfaced by the code-review dimensions; the validators still return []); nothing is gated.

edgeCases.input: ER class with no attributes, or an entity with no identifier slot.

edgeCases.expected: Mermaid source is sanitised per diagram type (identifiers aliased, labels quoted/escaped); HTML tables escape &, <, >, " so no markup is injected.

edgeCases.input: Sequence definition with recurse messages and truncations.
edgeCases.expected: Recursion keeps its 'recursion' note, truncations keep their Note over <participant>; messages table lists kind 'recurse' rows.

edgeCases.expected: Numbered markers go on key elements (inputs, actions, top-level text blocks, containers with a description); layout-only Columns are unnumbered and omitted from the table; numbering is depth-first and stable for the same definition.

edgeCases.input: A document carrying several definitions (ER + UX + sequence).
edgeCases.expected: Each companion page gets the same header values (one resolved CompanionHeader per finalize site) and differs only in title, kind badge, visual and description.

migration.stateBefore: Per s1 (c1, c2): the ER, sequence and component companions render via docgen assembleShell into a Mermaid page (ER as a classDiagram with inheritance arrows, sequence arrows labelled 'call') with an LLM narrative band and a back-link; the UX companion renders via renderUxMockDocument as a static card page without pan/zoom. Definitions carry no description/narrative fields. About 20 companion HTML files in the old format are committed under docs/.
migration.stateAfter: All four companions render through the companion-owned shell: header (project, work item, source doc, date, user), narrative (context line + optional per-visual narrative), one pan/zoom view panel, per-type description tables. Definitions accept optional description/narrative fields; their absence yields LOW findings. The docgen tool is unchanged. Existing committed companions stay in the old format until their artifact is re-finalized.

migrationSteps.action: Add optional description/narrative (and component path) fields to the four definition TS types, their *_PROPERTY_SCHEMA objects, AND the vendored closed schemas they are validated against (linkml-metamodel.schema.json, adaptive-cards.schema.json); existing stored definitions remain valid because every new field is optional.
Add the pan/zoom runtime asset under src/assets and include it in the copy-assets step so out/assets ships it next to the existing docgen Mermaid bundle.
Introduce the companion header resolver, page-content builders and the companion shell alongside the existing render path.
Switch the four render*Companion functions and the three orchestrator finalize sites to resolve a header and render through the new shell; stop calling docgen assembleShell from companion code.

Add per-kind completenessFindings (LOW only) and call them from the code-review diagram/ux dimensions; leave the validators' empty-when-sound contract unchanged; update the synthesizer content-gate rules to ask for descriptions and a narrative.

Remove the now-unused companion IR lowering functions (erDefinitionToIr, sequenceDefinitionToIr, componentDependencyDefinitionToIr, uxDefinitionToIr), the old renderUxMockDocument page wrapper, and the dead generateErCompanions seam (generate.ts + generate.test.ts), after confirming no remaining importers. Rewrite/trim/delete the companion __tests__ suites per the 'Companion test suites' inventory in the same change.

migration.backwardCompat: Internal surface only. The render*Companion functions keep their names, return type and CompanionArtifactRef shape; their opts gain a required `header` (all production callers are the three orchestrator finalize sites; the only other caller, the dead generateErCompanions seam, is removed, updated in the same change) and `sourceLink` is superseded by header.sourceDoc. Stored artifact JSON needs no rewrite: the new definition fields are optional. The VS Code review pane reads the projected definitions and only links companion files, so it is unaffected. The docgen tool keeps assembleShell unchanged.

alternativesConsidered.name: Companion shell + typed plug-in contract (off docgen)
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: A new companion-owned page shell takes a CompanionHeader + a CompanionPlugin output {visual, descriptionHtml, narrative}; each definition module exports its plug-in; docgen's assembleShell is no longer used by companions.
alternativesConsidered.approach: New module src/workflow/artifacts/companion/shell.ts exports renderCompanionPage(header: CompanionHeader, page: CompanionPageContent, runtime): string, where CompanionPageContent = { kindLabel, title, contextLine, narrative?, visual: {kind:'mermaid', source} | {kind:'html', html}, description: DescriptionBlock[] } and DescriptionBlock = {heading?, lead?, table: {columns, rows}} (cells are escaped text or a small tagged-token union, never raw HTML from the definition). Each of er.ts / ux.ts / sequence.ts / component.ts adds a pure toCompanionPage(def) returning CompanionPageContent (ER emits erDiagram Mermaid; sequence emits labelled autonumbered sequenceDiagram; component a flowchart; UX the existing card HTML plus numbered markers). A new header.ts resolves CompanionHeader {projectName, workItemId, sourceDoc{id, href}, date, user} with injectable clock + git/os lookups. render.ts's four functions keep their signatures but gain a required header option and call renderCompanionPage. A vendored transform-based pan/zoom script (src/assets/artifacts/companion/panzoom.js) is inlined for every page; mermaid stays inlined from src/assets/docgen. Definition types + *_PROPERTY_SCHEMA gain optional description/narrative; missing narrative/descriptions yield LOW findings (refined in §3.7: via completenessFindings, validators unchanged).
pros: Docgen tool is untouched (assembleShell, buildHtml, renderNarrativeBand unchanged).
Plug-ins are pure and return data, not HTML, so description tables are always escaped and unit-testable.
One place owns layout + pan/zoom, matching the approved mocks exactly.
render*Companion call sites in orchestrator change only by passing a header.
cons: Removes companions' use of the docgen oversized-diagram Graphviz fallback; very large diagrams rely on Mermaid alone.
IR lowering functions (erDefinitionToIr etc.) become dead for companions and must be removed or kept only for tests.

alternativesConsidered.name: Extend docgen assembleShell with a companion mode
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Add header/description/panel options to docgen's DocumentIR + buildHtml so companions and the docgen tool share one shell.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Widen NarratedContent with optional header + descriptionBlocks, teach buildHtml/assembleFallbackShell to render them when present, swap svg-pan-zoom for the transform runtime in both, add erDiagram emission to documentIRToMermaid, and lower UX into an html-visual IR variant. Companions keep calling assembleShell.
pros: Keeps the Graphviz oversized fallback for companions.
One shell for docgen and companions.
cons: Changes the docgen tool's output and its byte-identity tests; risk of regressing insrc_docgen.
Mixes workflow-specific header data (work item, source doc) into docgen's graph-derived IR, against the derived/narrated partition design.
UX would need a new non-graph IR variant in docgen.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Violates docgen no-regression and blurs the DocumentIR provenance partition, at L cost.

alternativesConsidered.name: String template file + slot substitution
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Ship companion.html as an asset with @@SLOT@@ placeholders (like src/assets/artifacts/templates) and fill them from each definition.
alternativesConsidered.approach: A bundled template with @@PROJECT@@, @@HEADER_TABLE@@, @@NARRATIVE@@, @@VISUAL@@, @@DESCRIPTION@@, @@RUNTIME@@ slots, loaded via a template loader with repo/user override layers; each definition module produces pre-rendered HTML fragments for its slots.
pros: Users could override the companion look per repo or per user.
Layout lives in one HTML file that designers can edit.
cons: Fragments are raw HTML strings, so escaping discipline is spread across modules.
Override layers add a lint + caching surface the spec did not ask for.
Harder to unit-test structure than typed content.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Workable but weaker on escaping discipline and adds override machinery the spec did not ask for.
